answer: Like an orchard where each tree must be tended for seasons before it bears fruit, an agent economy can make identity expensive in time rather than money: new agents earn trust only through a long history of verified work. A fresh identity starts with no pigment at all - no reputation, good or bad - and can only harvest timber-grade rewards after months of attested, useful contributions. A sybil farmer who must tend a hundred orchards for months before any payout finds the attack costs more than it earns.
